# Command reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run guide` (scripts/user-guide.ts). Don't edit by hand. -->

The help of every `catspec` command, as `catspec <command> --help` prints it. Exit codes: `0`
ok or warnings only, `1` errors found, `2` usage or config error, `3` internal error. With
`check --format agent`: `0` done, `2` not done (the agent is blocked), `1` error.

## catspec

```text
Usage: catspec [options] [command]

Specs bound to code: check that the code keeps the contracts of its specs.

Options:
  -V, --version                     output the version number
  --cwd <dir>                       run as if catspec was started in <dir>
  --config <file>                   use this config file instead of finding
                                    catspec.yaml
  --no-color                        print without colors
  --quiet                           print errors only
  --verbose                         print more detail
  -h, --help                        display help for command

Commands:
  init [options]                    create catspec.yaml,
                                    docs/spec/<example-feature>/ and the ADR log
                                    docs/architecture/adr/<name>-adr.md
  check [options] [paths...]        check the code against the specs: bindings,
                                    contracts and rules, by spec status;
                                    --specs-only checks the spec files only,
                                    --spec <id> reports one spec until DONE
  status [options] <spec> <status>  change a spec's status: ready needs its
                                    dependencies to exist, in-progress and
                                    implemented need them implemented and
                                    passing, implemented needs its own contracts
                                    to pass
  coverage [options]                contract satisfaction, enforcement coverage
                                    (manual rules and unenforced prose count
                                    against it) and reverse coverage (source
                                    files bound by a spec)
  list [options]                    list the specs
  show [options] <spec>             show one spec: its normalised model,
                                    dependencies, tasks and diagnostics
  graph [options]                   print the dependency graph of the specs
  baseline [options]                regenerate the lock files
                                    (<spec-id>.lock.json: what passed, where
                                    bindings resolved, their shapes) of every
                                    in-progress and implemented spec from the
                                    current code; this drops the ratchet history
  accept <spec>                     record the current shapes of a spec's bound
                                    declarations in its lock file, so an
                                    intended signature change is no longer
                                    reported as drift (CS0300)
  install-hooks [options]           install the pre-commit hook that runs
                                    `catspec check --staged`: in the git hooks
                                    folder (core.hooksPath included), or as an
                                    entry of husky or lefthook; a hook CatSpec
                                    didn't write is never overwritten without
                                    --force
  uninstall-hooks [options]         remove the pre-commit hook, and restore the
                                    hook it replaced
  sync [options]                    find renamed and moved declarations of
                                    bindings and fix the specs' locations
                                    (symbol and file only, never the contract);
                                    a dry run unless --apply. During a refactor
                                    it maps every binding of the refactor's
                                    baseline and, on success, ends the refactor
  refactor [options]                start a large refactor: record a baseline of
                                    every binding in the scope, so the hook
                                    groups their errors into one CS0215 and
                                    `catspec sync --apply` maps them all at the
                                    end
  bind [options] <symbol>           add a binding for an existing declaration to
                                    a spec, with its current shape (kind, bases,
                                    constructor dependencies, public members and
                                    their signatures) as the contract
  next [options] <feature>          what to do next for a feature (or a work
                                    item): the current workflow stage, its
                                    driver (skill, slash command, command), what
                                    to read, what to produce, its gates, and
                                    which work items are ready or waiting
  stage                             start or finish a workflow stage: run its
                                    gates, then apply its status (plan §D17)
  workflow                          inspect and validate the workflow profile
                                    (plan §D17)
  mcp                               start the MCP server on stdio, for AI
                                    agents: tools to read specs, check code
                                    against them and change spec locations (e.g.
                                    `claude mcp add catspec -- npx catspec mcp`)
  help [command]                    display help for command
```

## catspec init

```text
Usage: catspec init [options]

create catspec.yaml, docs/spec/<example-feature>/ and the ADR log
docs/architecture/adr/<name>-adr.md

Options:
  --name <name>      name of the ADR log (<name>-adr.md); default: the
                     repository folder name
  --preset <preset>  the SDD workflow to gate (default: detected from openspec/,
                     .specify/ or sdd-* skills, else catspec) (choices:
                     "catspec", "openspec", "spec-kit", "custom")
  --hooks            also install the pre-commit hook (see install-hooks)
  --agents           also add the CatSpec workflow block to AGENTS.md and the
                     Claude Code Stop hook to .claude/settings.json (existing
                     content is kept)
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## catspec check

```text
Usage: catspec check [options] [paths...]

check the code against the specs: bindings, contracts and rules, by spec status;
--specs-only checks the spec files only, --spec <id> reports one spec until DONE

Arguments:
  paths              only report diagnostics for these files or folders

Options:
  --specs-only       check spec files only: schema, ids, dependencies,
                     references, queries, layout, ADR ids
  --spec <id...>     check only these specs as if implemented; prints expected /
                     found / fix and DONE or NOT DONE
  --run-tests        run the tests of test rules with tests.command from
                     catspec.yaml
  --staged           check the commit being made (the pre-commit hook): read the
                     git index, check only the specs it touches, then update
                     their lock files
  --in-progress      check only the specs put in progress on this branch
                     (in-progress now, not where it left the default branch) as
                     if implemented; nothing to check when there are none
  --max-blocks <n>   with --format agent: let the agent stop after this many
                     blocks in a row with the same failures (default 3)
  --format <format>  output format (choices: "text", "json", "agent", default:
                     "text")
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## catspec status

```text
Usage: catspec status [options] <spec> <status>

change a spec's status: ready needs its dependencies to exist, in-progress and
implemented need them implemented and passing, implemented needs its own
contracts to pass

Arguments:
  spec        spec id
  status      the new status (choices: "draft", "ready", "in-progress",
              "implemented", "deprecated")

Options:
  --force     skip the dependency gate (an implemented spec must still pass)
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## catspec coverage

```text
Usage: catspec coverage [options]

contract satisfaction, enforcement coverage (manual rules and unenforced prose
count against it) and reverse coverage (source files bound by a spec)

Options:
  --format <format>  output format (choices: "text", "json", default: "text")
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## catspec list

```text
Usage: catspec list [options]

list the specs

Options:
  --status <status>  only specs with this status (choices: "draft", "ready",
                     "in-progress", "implemented", "deprecated")
  --ready            only specs that are ready to start: status ready,
                     dependencies implemented
  --format <format>  output format (choices: "text", "json", default: "text")
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## catspec show

```text
Usage: catspec show [options] <spec>

show one spec: its normalised model, dependencies, tasks and diagnostics

Arguments:
  spec               spec id

Options:
  --format <format>  output format (choices: "text", "json", default: "text")
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## catspec graph

```text
Usage: catspec graph [options]

print the dependency graph of the specs

Options:
  --format <format>  output format (choices: "mermaid", "dot", "json", default:
                     "mermaid")
  --focus <spec>     only this spec, its dependencies and its dependents
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## catspec baseline

```text
Usage: catspec baseline [options]

regenerate the lock files (<spec-id>.lock.json: what passed, where bindings
resolved, their shapes) of every in-progress and implemented spec from the
current code; this drops the ratchet history

Options:
  --rebuild   regenerate every lock file
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## catspec accept

```text
Usage: catspec accept [options] <spec>

record the current shapes of a spec's bound declarations in its lock file, so an
intended signature change is no longer reported as drift (CS0300)

Arguments:
  spec        spec id

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## catspec install-hooks

```text
Usage: catspec install-hooks [options]

install the pre-commit hook that runs `catspec check --staged`: in the git hooks
folder (core.hooksPath included), or as an entry of husky or lefthook; a hook
CatSpec didn't write is never overwritten without --force

Options:
  --manager <manager>  where to install the hook (choices: "auto", "git",
                       "husky", "lefthook", default: "auto")
  --force              keep an existing pre-commit hook as
                       pre-commit.catspec-backup and run it before CatSpec
  -h, --help           display help for command
```

## catspec uninstall-hooks

```text
Usage: catspec uninstall-hooks [options]

remove the pre-commit hook, and restore the hook it replaced

Options:
  --manager <manager>  where the hook is installed (choices: "auto", "git",
                       "husky", "lefthook", default: "auto")
  -h, --help           display help for command
```

## catspec sync

```text
Usage: catspec sync [options]

find renamed and moved declarations of bindings and fix the specs' locations
(symbol and file only, never the contract); a dry run unless --apply. During a
refactor it maps every binding of the refactor's baseline and, on success, ends
the refactor

Options:
  --apply            write the spec edits and moved lock entries (and stage
                     them)
  --staged           read the git index instead of the working tree
  --map <file>       a rename map: { "symbols": {…}, "namespaces": {…}, "paths":
                     {…} }
  --partial          with --apply: write what is mapped even if some bindings
                     are ambiguous or lost
  --update-mentions  with --apply: also rewrite backticked mentions of old names
                     in spec bodies
  --format <format>  output format (choices: "text", "json", default: "text")
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## catspec refactor

```text
Usage: catspec refactor [options] [command]

start a large refactor: record a baseline of every binding in the scope, so the
hook groups their errors into one CS0215 and `catspec sync --apply` maps them
all at the end

Options:
  --scope <glob...>  files in the refactor (default: the whole repository)
  --reason <text>    why, shown by the hook and `refactor status`
  --allow-wip        let commits with broken bindings through, on this branch
                     only
  -h, --help         display help for command

Commands:
  status [options]   show the refactor in progress: scope, branch, and the
                     bindings broken so far
  abort              drop the refactor in progress: its baseline is deleted, no
                     spec is changed
```

## catspec refactor status

```text
Usage: catspec refactor status [options]

show the refactor in progress: scope, branch, and the bindings broken so far

Options:
  --format <format>  output format (choices: "text", "json", default: "text")
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## catspec refactor abort

```text
Usage: catspec refactor abort [options]

drop the refactor in progress: its baseline is deleted, no spec is changed

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
```

## catspec bind

```text
Usage: catspec bind [options] <symbol>

add a binding for an existing declaration to a spec, with its current shape
(kind, bases, constructor dependencies, public members and their signatures) as
the contract

Arguments:
  symbol         the declaration: Name, Namespace.Name or path/to/module#Name

Options:
  --spec <id>    the spec to add the binding to
  --file <file>  only look in this file or glob (it is also written as the file
                 hint)
  -h, --help     display help for command
```

## catspec next

```text
Usage: catspec next [options] <feature>

what to do next for a feature (or a work item): the current workflow stage, its
driver (skill, slash command, command), what to read, what to produce, its
gates, and which work items are ready or waiting

Arguments:
  feature            a feature (folder name) or a spec id

Options:
  --format <format>  output format (choices: "text", "json", default: "text")
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## catspec stage

```text
Usage: catspec stage [options] [command]

start or finish a workflow stage: run its gates, then apply its status (plan
§D17)

Options:
  -h, --help                         display help for command

Commands:
  start [options] <stage> <target>   run the start gates of <stage> for a
                                     feature or a spec and, when they pass, set
                                     the status the stage sets at start; a
                                     per-spec stage given a feature runs for
                                     every spec
  finish [options] <stage> <target>  run the finish gates of <stage> for a
                                     feature or a spec and, when they pass, set
                                     the status the stage sets at finish; a
                                     per-spec stage given a feature runs for
                                     every spec
  help [command]                     display help for command
```

## catspec stage start

```text
Usage: catspec stage start [options] <stage> <target>

run the start gates of <stage> for a feature or a spec and, when they pass, set
the status the stage sets at start; a per-spec stage given a feature runs for
every spec

Arguments:
  stage              stage id from the workflow (catspec workflow show)
  target             a feature (folder name) or a spec id

Options:
  --force            start or finish even if gates fail or the stage is out of
                     order (logged); implemented still needs passing contracts
  --format <format>  output format (choices: "text", "json", default: "text")
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## catspec stage finish

```text
Usage: catspec stage finish [options] <stage> <target>

run the finish gates of <stage> for a feature or a spec and, when they pass, set
the status the stage sets at finish; a per-spec stage given a feature runs for
every spec

Arguments:
  stage              stage id from the workflow (catspec workflow show)
  target             a feature (folder name) or a spec id

Options:
  --force            start or finish even if gates fail or the stage is out of
                     order (logged); implemented still needs passing contracts
  --format <format>  output format (choices: "text", "json", default: "text")
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## catspec workflow

```text
Usage: catspec workflow [options] [command]

inspect and validate the workflow profile (plan §D17)

Options:
  -h, --help                display help for command

Commands:
  show [options] [feature]  list the stages, and where each feature (or the
                            given one) is
  doctor [options]          check the workflow config: skill files exist,
                            commands are installed, the preset matches the
                            repository
  snippet <stage>           print the lines to paste into a stage's skill, or
                            (agents) the AGENTS.md block for this workflow
  help [command]            display help for command
```

## catspec workflow show

```text
Usage: catspec workflow show [options] [feature]

list the stages, and where each feature (or the given one) is

Arguments:
  feature            a feature: also list each work item's stage

Options:
  --format <format>  output format (choices: "text", "json", default: "text")
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## catspec workflow doctor

```text
Usage: catspec workflow doctor [options]

check the workflow config: skill files exist, commands are installed, the preset
matches the repository

Options:
  --format <format>  output format (choices: "text", "json", default: "text")
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

## catspec workflow snippet

```text
Usage: catspec workflow snippet [options] <stage>

print the lines to paste into a stage's skill, or (agents) the AGENTS.md block

Arguments:
  stage       a stage id, or "agents"

Options:

```

## catspec mcp

```text
Usage: catspec mcp [options]

start the MCP server on stdio, for AI agents: tools to read specs, check code
against them and change spec locations (e.g. `claude mcp add catspec -- npx
catspec mcp`)

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command
```
